title: Churchill and Attlee: A Modest Man with Much to Be Modest About!
culture_region: India / Greece / USA / South Africa / World
summary: When a colleague praised Prime Minister Attlee as a remarkably modest man, Churchill famously quipped: 'He is a modest man, who has much to be modest about!'
keywords: Churchill and Attlee: A Modest Man with Much to Be Modest About!
full_text:
The British general election of July 1945 delivered one of the most stunning political upsets in modern history. Winston Churchill, the heroic wartime titan who had rallied the free world against Nazi Germany, was overwhelmingly rejected by the electorate in favor of the understated, quiet Labour leader Clement Attlee.

Churchill found himself abruptly relegated to Leader of the Opposition.

One afternoon in the parliamentary lobby, a conservative MP approached Churchill, seeking to offer polite praise of the new Prime Minister:
"Mr. Churchill, whatever our political differences with the Labour Party, one must admire Mr. Attlee's personal character. He is such an admirably modest gentleman!"

Churchill slowly removed his long Havana cigar, exhaled a thick cloud of blue smoke, and delivered his devastating verdict with characteristic gravelly wit:

**"A modest man, who has much to be modest about!"**

The corridor dissolved in laughter.

On another occasion, watching an empty taxi pull up outside the Houses of Parliament, Churchill deadpanned to bystanders:
"Look, an empty cab pulled up to the curb—and Clement Attlee got out!"

Despite these barbed quips, Churchill and Attlee shared deep mutual respect for each other's wartime partnership, illustrating how British parliamentary democracy thrived on merciless wit without destroying fundamental personal decency.
moral: Sharp political repartee can express fierce ideological disagreement without descending into personal hatred.
